title: The Standing of a Storage Agreement From Acceptance Through to Closing
content:
An agreement under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements is accepted into store once the paperwork is on file and the first bushels arrive, and only then does billing begin. This note sets out how its standing moves after that, and on what grounds it ends.

## The clauses

**Suspension of billing.** Billing is suspended while a disputed charge or a quality recheck is worked, for no longer than the programme's hold maximum counted in calendar days from the day the hold was set, and the days under suspension still count as days in store for the free-day and escalation clocks even though no charge is raised for them.

**Closing.** An agreement closes when the last bushel leaves and the account is clear, and a member with bushels still on hand cannot sign out.

**Termination by the elevator.** The elevator terminates an agreement of its own motion in only two cases: storage charges unpaid beyond the grace period after written notice, and grain going out of condition where the member declines conditioning. In both cases the grain is sold at the day's bid, the charges are taken out of the proceeds and the balance is paid to the member.

**Early termination by the member.** Early termination by the member carries the programme's early termination fee where the agreement has not run its minimum term, and needs the programme's notice in calendar days.

**Terminal standings.** Closed and terminated are both terminal; bushels brought back afterwards need a new agreement.

## Days under suspension

Suspension stops charges being raised. It does not stop the clocks: the days an agreement spends with billing suspended still count as days in store for the free-day clock and for the clock that decides when the rate steps up.

| During a suspension | |
| --- | --- |
| storage charges raised | none |
| days counted toward the free days | yes |
| days counted toward the point at which the rate steps up | yes |
| longest the suspension may run | the programme's hold maximum, in calendar days from the day the hold was set |

## The two grounds of termination by the elevator

| Ground | What follows |
| --- | --- |
| storage charges unpaid beyond the grace period, after written notice | the grain is sold at the day's bid, the charges come out of the proceeds and the balance is paid to the member |
| grain going out of condition where the member declines conditioning | the same: sold at the day's bid, charges out of the proceeds, balance to the member |

No other ground is one on which the elevator ends an agreement of its own motion.

## Basis questions answered

**A member with 3000 bushels still on hand asks to sign the agreement out.** Closing is for an agreement whose last bushel has left and whose account is clear, so a member with bushels still on hand does not sign out.

**A member ends an agreement that has not run its minimum term.** The programme's early termination fee stands, and the programme's notice in calendar days is what the early ending calls for.

**A member wants bushels put back under a terminated agreement.** Terminated is terminal, as closed is; bushels brought back afterwards need a new agreement.
